summary: Grays Harbor County, WA lookout site: a two-story lookout from 1942, an Aircraft Warning Service post, a state tower in 1959; gone by 1967 or 1969 (sources differ). Private timber land.

facts.design: R-6 14x14 foot cab on a two-story house; 1959 replacement was a 40-foot timber tower with live-in cab
facts.status_note: Lookout house and 1959 tower both gone; the register and Firelookout.com say gone by 1967, Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb say 1969; foundation block recorded in 1974

access.note: WillhiteWeb lists the landowner as a private timber company; no public access rights are described

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. WillhiteWeb describes a short dead-end Forest Service spur near the site.

facts.agency: Washington State Division of Forestry/DNR (Olympic National Forest ran the lookout before 1958)

events.note: Lookout first appears on 1930 and 1932 maps, per WillhiteWeb; builder not named
Two-story lookout with 14x14 cab, per a structural inventory quoted by Forest Lookouts and by WillhiteWeb; the register dates the first two-story house to 1943
Aircraft Warning Service station Baker 7-1 activated March 10, 1942; WillhiteWeb names observers Clarence and Marie Locke without dates
Quinault District manning the lookout during a dry period, per a May 18, 1956 Port Angeles Evening News item quoted by Forest Lookouts
Lookout turned over to the State
State (DNR) erected a 40-foot timber tower with live-in cab
Register and Firelookout.com say the 40-foot tower was gone by 1967
Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb say the tower was removed and the lookout house torn down in 1969
Foundation block of the lookout still there, per WillhiteWeb

notes_for_editor: Location conflict, unresolved: the record uses the FFLOS point (47.35465, -123.77034). Firelookout.com and FFLA give a point about 7.8 km west (47.35677, -123.86331). The sources read here give no coordinates, so the location is unchanged and needs a human check. Built date: the structural inventory quoted by Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb says 1942; the register says 1943. Removal: 1967 (register, Firelookout.com) vs 1969 (Forest Lookouts, WillhiteWeb); both are stated in the story. Height: the record's 3.0 m matches no source read (a two-story lookout of 20.7 ft per a benchmark note, and a 40-ft 1959 tower), so facts.height_m is left out. The record's R-6 design fits the WillhiteWeb cab description. Today's condition rests on a 1974 note and a 2017 caption, so nothing confirms what stands there now. Used 1 WebSearch and 6 page reads.
